chunks: As for what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abū Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ al-Asadī al-Naḥḥās, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

If a menstruating woman wears a garment and it remains on her until she becomes pure, then she should not perform salat in it until she washes it. If she has two garments upon her, she performs salat in the upper one of them. And if she has no garment other than one garment, then she should wash it when she menstruates, then wear it; then when she becomes pure she performs salat in it, even if she did not wash it.

This report may bear the meaning that we mentioned regarding the first report, and it may also be understood as being carried upon recommendation. What it contains in his saying, ‘She washes herself when she menstruates, then wears it; then when she becomes pure she performs salat in it, even if she did not wash it,’ indicates that menstruation itself does not render sweat impure, because if it were so, the state would not differ by washing before that. And that which indicates that this is to be understood as recommendation is what...
ai.seo_question: Does a garment worn during menstruation have to be washed before salat?
ai.summary: This text discusses the ruling of a garment worn by a menstruating woman and whether it must be washed before salat. It also indicates that menstruation itself does not make sweat impure, while suggesting that some wording in the report may be understood as expressing recommendation rather than obligation.
